note: The two redraft cases where a setting changes are no longer graded by wording patterns. A model reads what the answer says each named fact reads now (it sees the question, the answer and the fact names, nothing of the case's world), and code compares that reading with the world. The reader was measured first on 94 labelled sentences: 34 open ones read once and 60 held out, not read while its instructions were written, read three times; it took 0 of 43 stale sentences for current and refused 0 of 51 correct ones. Those sentences were written by an agent, not by the owner or a hostile reviewer. Grades that moved: g-scanning-off-reviews-same is right in 3 of 3 runs (2 of 3 before; one earlier run left scanning out). g-reviews-switched-off is unchanged: the redraft looked again and declined in 3 of 3, which is safe. New case g-reviews-switched-off-no-claim (no approved answer about reviews, the question names the repository): the redraft looked again and said main is not protected and no reviews are required, right in 3 of 3; its first version named no repository and was declined before any look, and was fixed in its own commit. Right cases: 32 of 37 (31 of 36). None ready and wrong. Checker: 22 labelled drafts were read again because the order of their sources is now part of the fingerprint and ten source ids were renamed so that none says its value or order; two new drafts where the later look reads protected, one sound and one stale, are read correctly in all eight readings. No defect missed, no sound draft objected to, of 56. Not a first look for the redraft cases: they were changed after reading earlier runs.
